title: Lamb Kebobs with Baby Arugula & Lemon Vinaigrette
description: Here’s a recipe that truly bridges the seasons. It’s inspired by winter’s hearty fare, but it’s also lighter, brighter, and freshened up with a spring ingredient like baby arugula. This might be good with a roasted tomato or eggplant on the side.
ingredients: 1/4 cup plus 1 Tbs. extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 lb. lamb tenderloins, or boneless lamb shoulder chops or lamb leg steaks, trimmed of extra fat and cut into 1-inch cubes (1-1/2 cups)
1/2 cup very thinly sliced red onion (1/2 small)
1/4 cup crumbled feta or blue cheese (1 oz.)
directions: Position an oven rack 4 inches from the broiler element and heat the broiler to high.
In a small bowl, combine the lemon juice, sour cream, garlic, and a pinch of salt. Slowly whisk in the 1/4 cup olive oil.

In a medium bowl, combine the lamb with the 1 Tbs. olive oil, 1/2 tsp. salt, and 1/4 tsp. pepper. Toss to coat evenly. Thread the lamb onto four small (8-inch) bamboo or metal skewers (maybe sticking some pieces of onion or even cherry tomatoes in between.)

Put the skewers on a broiler pan and broil the lamb, flipping once, until browned on the outside but still pink inside (medium doneness), 2 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer the skewers to a small, shallow baking dish. Whisk the vinaigrette to recombine and pour 3 Tbs. over the skewers, turning to coat.

In a medium bowl, toss the arugula and onion with enough of the remaining vinaigrette to lightly coat (you may not need it all). Season with salt and pepper to taste. Pile the greens on two plates, top each salad with two lamb skewers, sprinkle with the cheese, and serve immediately.
